title: Type I for Individuals: Nine Strategies for Awakening Your Motivation
coreMove: Personal Type I practices help you notice flow, define purpose, practice deliberately, renew energy, and remove motivational drains.

exampleSpecs.audience: Greta, a freelancer collecting evidence before redesigning her day
exampleSpecs.stakes: A workday feels busy but not alive.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the flow test as lived data.

exampleSpecs.audience: Jules, a design director protecting renewal before exhaustion
exampleSpecs.stakes: A studio calendar is full of client delivery and empty of creative renewal.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Apply the sabbatical lesson at a smaller scale.

exampleSpecs.audience: Samir, a writer using a prompt to escape a stale draft
exampleSpecs.stakes: A writing group is giving the same advice to the same stuck essay.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Oblique Strategies as a concrete pattern interrupt.

exampleSpecs.audience: Blythe, a graduate student mapping flow and frustration
exampleSpecs.stakes: A lab notebook contains data but no information about motivation.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Turn daily work into a motivation map.

exampleSpecs.audience: Kiran, a remote worker removing one avoidable drain
exampleSpecs.stakes: A home office reset risks adding tools while ignoring the real leak.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show a personal motivation audit leading to subtraction.

exampleSpecs.audience: Opal, a creative lead reclaiming a break as recovery
exampleSpecs.stakes: Lunch breaks are being swallowed by errands and status checks.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use renewal as part of the work system.
